text:
This looks like late 2019. The fed funds rate is 1.83%, after cuts in July, September and October 2019 that brought it to 1.50–1.75%, so the effective rate sits around 1.55% by November. A reading of 1.83% would fit September 2019, when the effective rate was about 1.90–2.00% after the September cut, or possibly October 2019. The 3-month change of -0.57 also points to a monthly average rate. Early-summer 2019 is about 2.40%, so a drop of 0.57 puts the current value at about 1.83%.

The other figures fit September or October 2019. The unemployment rate was 3.5% in September, so 3.7% suggests an earlier month, such as August (3.7%). Headline CPI at 1.76% fits August 2019 (1.75%), and core CPI at 2.39% also fits August 2019 (2.4%). The 10-year yield was 1.50% in August, though a monthly average could differ. The 10-year at 1.69 with a 1-month Treasury return of -1.2% suggests yields rose in the month, which fits September 2019, when the 10-year ended at 1.68%. Gold fell 3.6% in September 2019, which also fits. The unemployment rate in the data as then published was 3.7% in August (3.5% in September, released in October), so the snapshot is probably from end-September but with the unemployment rate not yet updated.

Overall I choose September 2019.
